Conversation, family & daily routines

perhaps adverb

also maybe, perchance, possibly

classical

Cic. Div. Caec. 40: fortasse dīcēs

1fortasse: short final e (Lewis & Short fortassē, without evidence). Catull. 85.1, Ōdī et amō. quārē id faciam fortasse requīris: the fifth foot, -tasse re-, is a dactyl. Also Hor. S. 1.3.20, 1.6.98. De Vaan 236, s.v. fors: “short final vowel”. Ruling: fortasse with a short final e.

fortasse1

adverb

maybe, perhaps

The everyday word of Cicero’s prose, with the indicative.

Examples

  • forsan et haec ōlim meminisse juvābit

    perhaps one day even this will be a pleasure to rememberVerg. A. 1.203

  • Fortasse.

    Maybe (as an answer).composed

  • Fortasse pluet; paenulam indue.

    Maybe it’ll rain; put your coat on.composed

  • Veniētne avia? — Fortasse.

    Is Grandma coming? — Maybe.composed

Other words

  • forsitan — perhaps

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 5: forsitan quaerātis

    From fors sit an; in Cicero always with the subjunctive.

  • forsan — perhaps

    adverb · also used · classical · Verg. A. 1.203

    (vōx plērumque poētica: Verg., Hor.; also post-Augustan prose)

  • fortassis — perhaps; the same word as fortasse, rarer

    adverb · also used · classical · Plaut.; Cic.; Hor.
